content: Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, has the potential to increase the plasma levels or pharmacological effects of drugs metabolized by the CYP3A4 enzyme. This effect can persist for up to 9 months following the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir. The increased drug levels may elevate the risk of adverse reactions associated with these substrates. Close monitoring is recommended when co-administering lenacapavir with CYP3A4 substrates. 1. Calcifediol: Lenacapavir may increase calcifediol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Cannabidiol: Lenacapavir may elevate cannabidiol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Exercise caution and monitor. 3. Capivasertib: Lenacapavir may increase capivasertib levels. Dose reduction of capivasertib is recommended when co-administered. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 4. Carbamazepine: Carbamazepine decreases lenacapavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 5. Cariprazine: Lenacapavir may increase cariprazine levels. Use caution and monitor. 6. Cenobamate: Cenobamate reduces lenacapavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Ceritinib: Lenacapavir may increase ceritinib levels. Use caution and monitor. 8. Chloroquine: Lenacapavir may elevate chloroquine levels. Use caution and monitor. 9. Chlorpheniramine: Lenacapavir may increase chlorpheniramine levels. Use caution and monitor. 10. Ciclesonide (inhaled and intranasal): Lenacapavir may increase ciclesonide levels. Use caution and monitor. 11. Cilostazol: Lenacapavir may elevate cilostazol levels. Use caution and monitor. 12. Cisapride: Lenacapavir may increase cisapride levels. Use caution and monitor. 13. Citalopram: Lenacapavir may elevate citalopram levels. Use caution and monitor. 14. Clarithromycin: Lenacapavir may increase clarithromycin levels. Use caution and monitor. 15. Clonazepam: Lenacapavir may elevate clonazepam levels. Use caution and monitor. 16. Clorazepate: Lenacapavir may increase clorazepate levels. Use caution and monitor. 17. Cobicistat: Lenacapavir may elevate cobicistat levels. Use caution and monitor. 18. Cobimetinib: Lenacapavir may increase cobimetinib levels. Use caution and monitor. 19. Cocaine (topical): Lenacapavir may elevate topical cocaine levels. Use caution and monitor. 20. Colchicine: Lenacapavir may increase colchicine levels. Use caution and monitor. 21. Conivaptan: Lenacapavir may elevate conivaptan levels. Use caution and monitor. 22. Conjugated Estrogens: Lenacapavir may increase conjugated estrogen levels. Use caution and monitor. 23. Copanlisib: Lenacapavir may elevate copanlisib levels. Use caution and monitor. 24. Cortisone: Lenacapavir may significantly increase cortisone levels, potentially leading to toxicities such as Cushing syndrome or adrenal suppression. Initiate dexamethasone at the lowest dose, monitor, and titrate accordingly. 25. Crizotinib: Lenacapavir may increase crizotinib levels. Use caution and monitor. 26. Cyclophosphamide: Lenacapavir may elevate cyclophosphamide levels. Use caution and monitor. 27. Cyclosporine: Lenacapavir may increase cyclosporine levels. Use caution and monitor. 28. Dabigatran: Lenacapavir may elevate dabigatran levels. Refer to prescribing information for guidance on co-administration. Use caution and monitor. 29. Dabrafenib: Lenacapavir may increase dabrafenib levels. Conversely, dabrafenib reduces lenacapavir levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 30. Daclatasvir: Lenacapavir may elevate daclatasvir levels. Use caution and monitor. 31. Danicopan: Danicopan increases lenacapavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor. 32. Dantrolene: Lenacapavir may increase dantrolene levels. Use caution and monitor. 33. Dapsone: Lenacapavir may elevate dapsone levels. Use caution and monitor. 34. Daridorexant: Lenacapavir may increase daridorexant levels. Use caution and monitor. 35. Darifenacin: Lenacapavir may elevate darifenacin levels. Use caution and monitor. 36. Darolutamide: Lenacapavir may increase darolutamide levels. Use caution and monitor. 37. Darunavir: Lenacapavir may elevate darunavir levels. Use caution and monitor. 38. Dasatinib: Lenacapavir may increase dasatinib levels. Use caution and monitor. 39. Deflazacort: Lenacapavir may elevate deflazacort levels. Reduce deflazacort dosage to one-third of the recommended dose (e.g., reduce 36 mg/day to 12 mg/day). Modify therapy and monitor closely. 40. Dexamethasone: Lenacapavir may increase dexamethasone levels. Use caution and monitor. This list highlights the need for careful monitoring and potential dose adjustments when lenacapavir is co-administered with drugs metabolized by CYP3A4 or P-glycoprotein.
